# Organizr

> Organizr is an all-in-one personal planner and habit tracker for iPhone, Android, Mac and Windows. Habits, workouts, nutrition, body measurements, goals, finances and personal projects live in one hub, synced across devices with end-to-end encryption and analyzed by a built-in AI.

## What is Organizr

Organizr replaces the handful of separate apps most people use to run their personal life. In a single app you get a kanban board, a habit tracker, a workout log, a food diary, body measurement tracking, goal management, a wallet with accounts and investments, a subscription tracker, a recipe collection, a wardrobe organizer, a reading library and a file organizer. Every section shares data with the others, so a workout logged on the phone shows up in the tracker, the dashboards and the AI analysis.

## Platforms

- iPhone (iOS) — [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/organizr/id6790398372)
- Android
- macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), macOS 12 or later
- Windows 10 / 11
- Apple Watch — log workouts, spending and habits from the wrist

## Key features

- **Tracker** — daily habit tracker with streaks, statistics and a unified dashboard
- **Board** — personal kanban for tasks and projects with customizable columns
- **Workout** — training log with sets, reps and load progression; compares each session to the previous one; Hevy integration
- **Nutrition** — food diary with calories and macronutrients; FatSecret integration
- **Recipes** — personal recipe collection, usable for meal planning and readable by Organizr AI
- **Measurements** — body weight, BMI and measurement tracking over time
- **Goals** — goal setting on 3-month cycles or a full year, with milestone tracking
- **Wallet** — accounts, transactions and investments with spending dashboards
- **Subscriptions** — subscription and renewal tracking, including shared subscriptions
- **Wardrobe** — clothing you own, want or plan to sell (desktop only)
- **Reading** — personal library with reading status, summaries and notes
- **Files** — see where your files live across machines and when backups need updating (desktop only)
- **Organizr AI** — reads the data you already track and turns it into workout plans, recipe analysis and insights on habits, nutrition and spending
- **Sync** — end-to-end encrypted sync across iPhone, Android, Mac and Windows
- **Time Analyzr** — time and progress analysis across sections

## Integrations

- **Hevy** — import workouts
- **FatSecret** — import meals and nutritional values ([setup guide](https://organizr.it/fatsecret-sync-tutorial/))

## Plans and pricing

- **Organizr Lite** — free. 1 unlimited board, up to 6 subscriptions, 3 workout routines, 6 recipes, wallet with 1 account, full tracker, food diary, Apple Watch workouts, 50 Organizr AI credits per month. No advanced dashboards, no device sync, no Time Analyzr.
- **Organizr Pro, monthly** — €3.49/month
- **Organizr Pro, annual** — €17.99/year (from €24.99). Everything with no limits, advanced dashboards, device sync, Time Analyzr, wardrobe and file organization on desktop, 300 Organizr AI credits per month.
- **Organizr Lifetime** — €49.99 one-time (from €89.99). All Pro features forever, no renewals, 300 Organizr AI credits per month for 24 months.

Prices are also shown in USD on the site. No account is required to use Organizr Lite.

## Privacy and data

Your data lives on your devices. Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted: only the last 90 days are held on the server, encrypted, purely to keep devices aligned. Organizr has no access to the content of your data.

## Blog articles

### Habits

- [Ninety-day goals beat New Year resolutions](https://organizr.it/blog/90-day-goals-beat-resolutions/) — A year is too long to stay accountable and a week is too short to change anything. Why a quarter is the unit that fits both training and life.
- [How to build a gym habit that survives week three](https://organizr.it/blog/gym-habit-that-lasts/) — Week one is easy, week three is where gym habits die. What to change in the plan, the schedule and the tracking so the habit outlives motivation.
- [Habit stacking: bolt the new habit onto one you already have](https://organizr.it/blog/habit-stacking/) — New habits fail because they have no trigger. Anchor them to something already automatic, like coffee or the commute, and the trigger comes free.
- [The morning routine myth: three habits that actually move the needle](https://organizr.it/blog/morning-routine-myth/) — Cold plunges and 5am alarms are content, not results. Three morning habits that actually help, and how to keep them when the week goes sideways.
- [Motivation runs out. Systems don’t.](https://organizr.it/blog/motivation-vs-systems/) — Motivation is a mood, and moods are a bad foundation. How to replace it with defaults, friction and a record you can look at when you do not feel like it.
- [Sleep is a training variable, not a reward](https://organizr.it/blog/sleep-is-a-training-variable/) — Strength, appetite and adherence all track sleep. What short sleep does to a training block, and the handful of habits that fix most of it.
- [Why streaks break, and the two-day rule that saves them](https://organizr.it/blog/two-day-rule-streaks/) — One missed day costs nothing. Two in a row is how habits die. The rule that makes a broken streak recoverable instead of final.
- [What a year of training actually costs](https://organizr.it/blog/what-a-year-of-training-costs/) — Membership, supplements, kit, the coach you used for two months and the subscriptions you forgot. A full year priced out, and where the waste usually is.

### Training

- [Cardio and weights in the same week without losing strength](https://organizr.it/blog/cardio-and-weights-same-week/) — The interference effect is real but smaller than the internet thinks. How to order sessions, space them out and pick the cardio that costs you least.
- [Deload weeks: backing off on purpose before your body does it for you](https://organizr.it/blog/deload-weeks/) — Stalled lifts, sore joints and dread are late signals. How to schedule a deload, what to cut and what to keep, and how to come back stronger than you left.
- [Training at home or at the gym: an honest comparison](https://organizr.it/blog/home-gym-vs-gym/) — What a home setup really costs, what it can and cannot replace, and the training goals where the gym is still worth the trip.
- [How many rest days you actually need](https://organizr.it/blog/how-many-rest-days/) — Recovery is not the same for a beginner, a lifter on a cut and someone sleeping five hours. The signals that say rest, and the ones that just say lazy.
- [How to log a workout so the data is useful six months later](https://organizr.it/blog/how-to-track-a-workout/) — Sets and reps are not enough. The fields worth logging, the ones that waste your time, and how to keep the log fast enough that you keep doing it.
- [Progressive overload, explained without a spreadsheet](https://organizr.it/blog/progressive-overload-explained/) — Adding weight is only one of five ways to overload a lift. How to progress reps, sets, tempo and range of motion, and how to know when you actually did.
- [Push pull legs or full body: which split fits your week](https://organizr.it/blog/push-pull-legs-vs-full-body/) — The best split is the one you can repeat on a bad week. How to choose between full body, upper lower and push pull legs based on days, not on theory.
- [The scale lies: the measurements that tell the truth](https://organizr.it/blog/scale-weight-lies/) — Daily weight swings two kilos on water alone. Waist, photos, lifts and weekly averages are what actually show whether the plan is working.
- [Zone 2, steps and NEAT: the boring cardio that works](https://organizr.it/blog/zone-2-steps-neat/) — Most of the cardio that changes your body is slow, dull and uncounted. What zone 2 actually feels like, and why a step target beats another HIIT class.
